Election results

By Jane Doe

Voters in the capital chose a new parliament on Sunday, in an election that observers described as the most closely watched in a decade. Turnout reached 71 percent, well above the figure recorded four years ago.

The governing coalition lost its majority after the opposition alliance won 212 of 450 seats, according to the electoral commission. Coalition talks are expected to begin early next week and could take several weeks to conclude.

Analysts said the result reflects dissatisfaction with rising living costs and a long-running dispute over energy policy. "People wanted change, and they said so clearly," one political scientist told DW on Monday.

International observers reported only minor irregularities and praised the orderly conduct of polling stations across the country. The final official result is due on Thursday.
